subject: visualizing an nrrd average brain image in nat with im3d

messages.author: c0c6c70c50a5ee22
messages.subject: visualizing an nrrd average brain image in nat with im3d
parts:
Hello!

I have been working for a while on registering zebrafish telencephalon brain images and creating an average from those registrations using cmtk on the command line. Now I am at a point where I have generated and average .nrrd file and have registered each original brain to that average so that I can begin warping the neuron objects accordingly. Using nat package, I have been able to import the swc neuron files (which I exported from Imaris) and transform them by the registration .list files. However, what I am unsure about is how to import the average brain image so I can plot a 3d representation of the surface and then graph the neurons on top of that. Is this what I should be using im3d for or is there a better way to visualize the average brain image and neurons on a 3d plot? I do not have access to Amira and when I import the transformed swc files back into Imaris they are always outside of the boundaries of the average image files so I am unsure of how to proceed.

Thanks!

Max

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] visualizing an nrrd average brain image in nat with im3d
parts:
Hi Max,

Sounds like you’ve made great progress. 

I would strongly suggest making a surface object model of your average template brain. I do this in Amira but there are surely alternatives. You should aim for a model without too many vertices (think 20000) and make sure that you smooth the input image data and / or surface model. If you cannot do this all in Imaris, the free software meshlab has good options for model reduction and smoothing.

To check that things are behaving in the meantime, you can plot the bounding box of your average brain in R and seeing how the neurons look wrt to that. 

avgbrain=as.templatebrain(“avgbrain.nrrd”)
plot3d(avgbrain)
plot3d(myneurons)

(Unchecked)

Now as for the discrepancy between your swcs and you’re me average brain in imaris, there are a couple of possibilities I can think of:

1. That imaris ignores the voxel spacing of the image when plotting the transformed swcs (ie assumes that swcs are in raw pixel software). I have seen some other software do this, although I would be surprised.

2. The transformation did not go to plan. The most likely possibility being that the neurons need to be transformed in the opposite direction. 

Just plotting all of the neurons in R as above should give you a hint if 2 is true. 

All the best,

Greg.

How did you make your raw tracings? Is it possible that they are in raw pixel coordinates not in spatially calibrated coordinates? If so you would need to multiply the neuronlist that you read by the raw voxel dimensions for the images that you used for tracing. You can use the Fiji simple neurite tracer plugin to overlay the raw swc and raw image if you don’t have another option to check. Best, Greg.

On Wed, Nov 6, 2019 at 11:39 AM Greg Jefferis <jeff...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Max,

We have a simple hack to make it easier to plot surfaces for template brains. For every template brain called e.g. 

JFRC2

We also provide a surface object called

JFRC2.surf

Now there are 2 things you need to do

1. Read your STL data into R
2. Convert it into an “hsxurf” object with a suitable name

There is a function in the rgl library that should work for STL, but I have never used it. In theory it should be as simple

library(nat)
x=readSTL("average.stl", plot=FALSE)
average.surf=as.hxsurf(x)
plot3d(average)

The readSTL function looks a little hacky so you may run into trouble. Alternatively, can you export as obj or ply? These are also very common surface mesh formats. You can also convert STL to OBJ in Meshlab.

Best,

Greg.
